mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) reduces the discount rate applied to equity cash flows, increasing the present value of future earnings and driving positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS level shows no correlation with 20-day forward returns (Rank IC < 0.03) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.3 percentage points over three months signals labor market deterioration and economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate broad-based demand contraction, triggering negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns through reduced consumer spending expectations.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS decline in the last month
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS does not lead to negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles, an increase in federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals aggressive policy that suppresses economic activity and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: In monetary tightening cycles, FEDFUNDS increases do not lead to negative 20-day returns (i.e., returns are positive in > 60% of cases).

mechanism_narrative: Higher industrial production (INDPRO) reflects robust manufacturing output and supply chain strength, supporting corporate earnings growth and driving positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: INDPRO level shows no positive correlation with 60-day forward returns (Rank IC < 0.03) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.5 percentage points over three months signals imminent monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns through yield curve inversion expectations.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5pp in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A deceleration in employment growth (PAYEMS) combined with rising unemployment (UNRATE) indicates labor market weakness, triggering negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns through reduced consumer confidence and spending.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth rate declines and UNRATE rises in the last month
failure_condition: The joint signal of PAYEMS deceleration and UNRATE rise does not produce negative 5-day returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, a slowdown in quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) signals economic peak and impending slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns through reduced earnings growth expectations.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansions, a slowdown in GDPC1 does not lead to negative 60-day returns (i.e., returns are positive in > 60% of cases).
